study.question: Does allowing already-available static context to modify history retrieval help beyond the incumbent target-category/brand queries, and does any benefit require target-dependent field selection? Observed structural limitation: candidate.py routes all other static fields only to the output MLP. Observed full-population seed-42 AUCs: static .6050036145, pooled .6102261137, DIN-style .6133619861; current aligned/shared .6185212237 versus aligned/separate .6185023675, crossed/shared .6180263406, crossed/separate .6181363361. Thus correspondence is promising, while separate routing has no observed advantage; uncertainty is unresolved without repetitions.
study.hypothesis: Residual queries conditioned on non-category/non-brand static fields can retrieve different useful behavior evidence for different user/ad contexts. Target-conditioned context attention should outperform both mean context and target-blind learned context selection if target-specific field relevance is the operative mechanism. This is a falsifiable prospective local hypothesis, not established by the structural limitation or industry results. Zero new trainable parameters are added: the existing nonlinear scorer is reused for context and history, so tied-gradient interference is a substantive implementation risk.

nearest_work.source_ref: queryformer-paper-v1, arXiv:2609.16548v1, archived content SHA256 27673f600e2ebec40e365fc313871564fba4b3671c4ea65270bca8f8b1123473; text lines 128-247, sections 4.2 and 5.2 Table 4
nearest_work.difference: Inherit the general idea of contextual attention-generated retrieval queries. The source initializes probes from pooled behavior, refines user/item tokens, retrieves per-domain evidence and uses multiple attention blocks/views and a different optimizer/loss. Here target category/brand anchors attend only to existing other static embeddings using the incumbent nonlinear scorer, add a fixed .5 residual, then use the unchanged shared field-history attention and 24 statistics. No additional probes, projections, tokens, history, auxiliary labels or trainable parameters. Uniform, zero-anchor learned selection and exact-query replacement controls isolate a small local transfer; neither source reproduction nor novelty is claimed.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit target-aware local relevance and embedding/MLP reference. The local host reference uses masked normalized softmax, whereas DIN explicitly abandons softmax normalization to retain activation intensity. This study preserves the local normalized reference and does not claim to reproduce DIN. The changed mechanism is static-context query residuals, not unnormalized attention.

Retain all parameter constructors, field correspondence, shared score routing, pooling dimension and evidence statistics. Add only a parameter-tied static-context path into the category/brand retrieval queries; all four variants share identical code except literal query_context config.

study.proposed_difference: For each target field f, let C contain only nonzero supplied static IDs at positions other than category and brand. Reuse s(q,e)=attention([q,e,q-e,q*e]). Adaptive uses a_f=masked_softmax(s(q_f,e_j)); blind uses masked_softmax(s(0,e_j)) shared across the two fields; uniform uses 1/|C|. Selected contexts form q_f_prime=q_f+0.5*c_f before unchanged history scoring. Target control sets q_f_prime=q_f exactly. Empty C yields zero context, empty supplied histories still pool to exact zero. All four modes compute all context alternatives without changing constructor/RNG order; only the residual selector differs. Parameter count and data passes match; backward work can differ and measured cost must be reported. Source/config hashes and checks are added to variant notes before delivery. Novelty remains unverified; this is a controlled adaptation of a known query-generation principle.
predictions: Primary contrast: query_adaptive exceeds query_uniform and query_blind in full-population validation ROC-AUC; total utility additionally requires exceeding query_target. No significance or mechanism conclusion from one seed.

Query-target predictions should reproduce the historical parent under the same host seed/recipe, subject to host nondeterminism. It has identical trainable computation and parameter initialization; auxiliary disconnected computations affect wall time only.

Descriptive first-512 diagnostics should show nonzero context availability and query updates; adaptive weights should differ from uniform/blind and produce nonzero pool distances from unchanged queries. These checks establish execution, not predictive utility or semantic relevance.

All-padding histories, missing static context and missing target IDs produce finite predictions; context padding gets zero attention. No-context queries equal their original targets in every mode; pooled history is zero for empty histories.

Report host whole-population AUC/Logloss and existing history-length, action-composition, hour, training-frequency and missing-field slices with sample/positive/negative counts. Slice comparisons are exploratory; no custom slice labels or prediction access are available in this phase.
falsifiers: If adaptive does not improve over uniform/blind after paired repetitions, target-specific field selection is unsupported even if all contextual variants improve over target.
If adaptive does not improve over target control, this tied-scorer residual implementation has no demonstrated utility; do not refute all contextual-query architectures.

If contextual weights or query/pool distances are numerically zero with available nonzero fields, the proposed mechanism was not implemented/activated; an AUC difference then requires another explanation.
If target-control behavior materially differs from the parent beyond nondeterminism, inspect source/API/initialization before interpreting other variants.
Any information-boundary violation, nonfinite output or trial-cap overrun is an invalid/failed run, not scientific counterevidence. Preserve charged failures and do not duplicate unknown executions.
alternative_explanations: Larger target-query magnitude or generic static residuals, rather than adaptive field relevance; uniform and blind replacements address these only partially. No semantic relevance follows from attention weights.

An apparent benefit may be parameter sharing as regularization, new gradient routes to static embeddings, or embedding-norm effects. Same parameter count is not a proof of the retrieval explanation. A later stop-gradient or separate-scorer control would be needed if consequential.

A null can reflect scorer interference between static-field and history roles, fixed gain .5, incompatible field embedding geometry or insufficient three-epoch optimization. Inspect diagnostics before proposing a distinct follow-up; do not tune against test.

The earlier r0000 2x2 showed target matching useful while support-only rate/count did not exceed DIN (.6129227872/.6133185009 versus .6133619861); matching rate/count reached .6163503542/.6167540723. r0001 aligned event-time matching .6171490323 exceeded duplicate .6166311410, factorized .6162595069 and activity .6166033784. These motivate preserving explicit target/time features but are single-seed local observations.

r0002 same-event joint category-brand evidence .6183522161 did not beat factorized .6183741960 or support .6184566652; duplicate .6180129980 also improved relative to the earlier parent. Hence added shape/optimization and generic support can explain gains; do not resurrect a proven joint-synergy claim.

r0003 global-mean .6178996264, global-attention .6178267412, action-mean .6178636332 and action-attention .6179337371 all underperformed r0002-support_pair .6184566652. Action-specific content preservation was executed but unhelpful in that implementation, despite pv dominance in first-512 diagnostics. The current study does not append action summaries or larger readout features.

r0004 correct-versus-crossed query contrasts favor field correspondence, but separate/shared interaction is small and raw separate routing did not win. Avoid selecting a more complex field router on the basis of attention-weight distance.

No failed host trials appear among the 23 allowed observation IDs; negative/null branches above remain recorded. Missing Torch/private data in the coding workspace is a capability limit, not an experiment failure. Agent memory search returned no scoped records; own-arm supplied immutable trial receipts are the available observation provenance.

Seed noise, repeated validation selection, user clustering and static snapshot as-of ambiguity remain. Source pCVR results, row-group split, behavior domains and extra supervision do not transfer automatically. No withheld assessment is available.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Local target awareness improves over pooled histories, correspondence helps, separate field routing does not win, and source inspection shows other static fields cannot affect history weights. This motivates a small test of contextual query formation, while the actual bottleneck remains unestablished.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: Replace behavior-initialized, multi-block projected query generation by two target-anchored residual context queries using the existing nonlinear scorer over available other static fields, with zero added parameters and fixed .5 gain.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: QueryFormer arXiv:2609.16548v1 sections 4.2.1-4.2.5 and 5.2 Table 4, archived exact-version primary text read. No co-transformer, behavior-initialized probes, extra views, dense projections, auxiliary conversion-time loss or optimizer changes. Source ablation changes architecture/capacity; no source metric transfers to this task. Novelty unverified.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: Adaptive fails to beat both mean and zero-anchor selection; if none beat target, local contextual-query utility is unsupported.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Only organizer summary is supplied; group-exchange/old-history compression does not follow from current evidence. Earlier action summaries underperformed the support parent; supplied history is fixed and rare-action data are sparse in first-512 diagnostics.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: None adopted; no older-history expansion, compression, per-domain branches or exchange gates.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Organizer-only external report, detailed original implementation and component effects unverified. Action types are not equivalent to source domains; this study changes static query conditioning only.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: A later permitted matched-history local-versus-old replacement with sufficient support could motivate reassessment; current proposal provides no UniDAC mechanism test.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Token allocation is a possible bottleneck but no local field-wise utility or capacity allocation evidence is available. Adding tokens would confound this parameter-preserving query study.
